negotiation:
Response format is chosen by content negotiation: pass `?format=json` to
request a JSON response, or send an `Accept: application/json` header with
no `format` param present. Omitting both, or an Accept header that doesn't
prefer JSON, returns the HTML page. `?format=json` wins outright whenever
present, taking priority over the Accept header even when its own value
isn't recognized. `format` is a declared parameter (available on every
endpoint) whose only valid value is `json`; any other explicit value is a
validation error -- but because a non-`json` format value is itself read
as "this request does not want JSON," that error surfaces on the HTML page
(the message shown inline), never as a JSON error body. If you need format
mistakes to be script-visible, omit `format` and negotiate purely via the
`Accept` header.
locale:
Pass `?locale=` naming one of the served locales to select the response's
language (see the Locales section below for the current list). Locale
affects VALUES only: `label` text, free-text descriptive fields, and error
messages resolve in the requested locale, while every `id`, object key, and
enum value stays the same fixed English string regardless of locale -- a
client can index into the same key path and switch on the same ids whether
it requested any served locale. `locale` is a declared parameter (available
on every endpoint); a value naming a locale sask doesn't serve is a
validation error (`error.invalid_locale`).
id_label:
Any field representing a localizable domain value (a body name, eclipse
type, season, event, House, fixed star, or lunar-calendar id) renders as an
object with two keys: `id`, an invariant, English, machine-stable identifier
safe to use as a database key, a switch/case value, or a UI class name; and
`label`, the human-readable text resolved for the request's locale. Only
`label` changes across locales -- `id` never does. Free-text fields the
engine already resolved to a display string (notes, rings description,
night_summary, image_prompt, lore date/time, and a scene body's
direction/color/phase) are plain localized strings with no separate id,
since the underlying message unit does not carry one to switch on.
temporal_contract:
Every response carries the resolved moment expressed in every calendar this
system tracks -- as `query` (on /, /moons, /planets, /sky) or as
`parameters.start` / `parameters.end` (on /ephemeris): `pulse` (the atomic
integer time unit), `astro_day` and `astro_time` (the invariant civil
calendar), `orbital_position`, and both `fatunik_date` and `terpin_date`
(the two in-world civil calendars). This is always present regardless of
which input form the request supplied (pulse, astro_day, or a calendar
date) -- the server resolves the moment once and reports every
representation, so a client never needs to convert calendars itself. /sky
and /ephemeris additionally carry lore-language time/date strings when
lore_time is enabled in server config.
error_envelope:
A failed request -- malformed input, a value outside a declared constraint,
an unknown parameter, or the ephemeris throttle -- returns HTTP 400 with a
JSON body shaped `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. `code` is
a stable, English, locale-invariant identifier safe to match on in client
code, drawn from the same i18n tag that produces `message` with its
`error.` prefix stripped. `message` is the human-readable, locale-resolved
explanation. See the Error Codes section below for the complete catalog of
codes this API can return.
integration_guidance:
Distilled from real integration friction (DEBT-0006):

1. Query by whichever calendar input you already have -- `pulse`,
   `astro_day` (+ optional `time_of_day`), or a Fatunik/Terpin date triple
   -- the server resolves ONE moment and reports it back in every
   representation, so you never need to convert calendars client-side.
2. /ephemeris throttles both ends: `step_minutes` cannot go below the
   server's configured step floor, and the total range cannot exceed its
   configured range cap -- requesting outside those bounds is a validation
   error (`error.ephemeris_range_invalid`), never a silently-clamped
   result. See the /ephemeris parameter descriptions below for this
   deploy's actual limits.
3. /ephemeris's range end is either a raw `end_pulse` OR a `duration_days`
   relative to `start` -- never a full calendar-date end, unlike `start`,
   which accepts any of the four moment forms.
4. Build your UI or downstream logic against `id`, never against `label`
   text -- `label` changes with locale, `id` never does.
5. An empty-string query parameter value is treated identically to an
   absent parameter everywhere in this API -- `?pulse=` is the same as
   omitting `pulse`.
6. `/` only accepts `pulse` as input (not astro_day or a calendar date) --
   unlike /moons, /planets, and /sky, which accept all four moment forms.

shared_parameters.name: format
shared_parameters.description: Content-negotiation override (DD-0026): format=json forces a JSON response regardless of the Accept header.

shared_parameters.name: locale
shared_parameters.description: Locale toggle (DD-0022): must name a locale sask serves (see /help).

/.description:
Resolves a single moment (via `pulse` only -- this endpoint does not accept
astro_day or calendar-date input) and returns its temporal contract: the
pulse, Astro day/time, orbital position, and both civil calendar dates.

parameters.name: pulse
parameters.description: Raw pulse count. Rounded to the nearest integer pulse.

error.message: Se requiere un parámetro de pulso, astro_day o fecha de calendario.

/ephemeris.description:
Resolves a start moment (the full moment resolution, prefixed `start_`)
and a range end (either a raw `end_pulse` or a `duration_days` relative to
start), then returns a time series of sky scenes stepped by
`step_minutes` across that range, in a `scribal` (lore-language scenes),
`kinematic` (compact per-body numeric data), or `both` profile.

parameters.name: end_pulse
parameters.description: Ephemeris range end, as a raw pulse count (selects pulse mode; mutually exclusive with duration_days).

parameters.name: duration_days
parameters.description: Ephemeris range length in days from start (selects date mode; mutually exclusive with end_pulse).

parameters.name: step_minutes
parameters.description: Ephemeris series step size, in Astro minutes. Required whenever any ephemeris field is submitted. Subject to the ephemeris throttle's step floor (config/ephemeris_data.toml).

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Which series to render: lore-language scenes (scribal), compact per-body numeric data (kinematic), or both.

pulse.name: start_pulse
pulse.description: Raw pulse count. Rounded to the nearest integer pulse.

astro_day.name: start_time_of_day
astro_day.description: Civil time-of-day within an Astro Day, paired with astro_day. Range 00:00:00-23:59:59.

fatunik_date.name: start_fatunik_year
fatunik_date.description: Fatunik calendar year, paired with fatunik_month and fatunik_day.

fatunik_date.name: start_fatunik_month
fatunik_date.description: Fatunik calendar month, paired with fatunik_year and fatunik_day.

fatunik_date.name: start_fatunik_day
fatunik_date.description: Fatunik calendar day, paired with fatunik_year and fatunik_month.

terpin_date.name: start_terpin_year
terpin_date.description: Terpin calendar year, paired with terpin_month and terpin_day.

terpin_date.name: start_terpin_month
terpin_date.description: Terpin calendar month, paired with terpin_year and terpin_day.

terpin_date.name: start_terpin_day
terpin_date.description: Terpin calendar day, paired with terpin_year and terpin_month.
